IV. 1,4-Dihydronaphthalene-1,4-endoxide formed by Diels-Alder [4+2] cycloaddition
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (o-Chlorotoluene + KNH2 in liquid NH3): Deprotonation and chloride loss produces 2,3-dehydrotoluene (a substituted benzyne); nucleophilic attack of amide ion (NH2-) occurs with equal ease at both ends of the triple bond. Therefore, A corresponds to III.
Step 2: Match item B (Chlorobenzene-1-[14C] + NaNH2 in liquid NH3): Elimination of HCl forms benzyne with the labeled carbon involved in the formal triple bond; subsequent addition of NH3 occurs equally at C-1 and C-2, giving exactly 50:50 isotopic distribution. Therefore, B corresponds to I.
Step 3: Match item C (Benzyne generated in the presence of Furan): The strained alkyne bond in benzyne has high reactivity, acting as an extremely potent dienophile that traps furan in a [4+2] concerted cycloaddition. Therefore, C corresponds to IV.
Step 4: Match item D (2-Bromobenzoic acid + heat with isoamyl nitrite (anthranilic acid method)): Diazotization of anthranilic acid produces a zwitterionic diazonium carboxylate that decomposes cleanly into gaseous CO2, N2, and reactive benzyne. Therefore, D corresponds to II.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II, which corresponds to Option B.

subject: Chemistry
questionText:
Match the Birch reduction systems in List I with their exact diene products and regiochemical rationale in List II:
List I:
A. Anisole (Methoxybenzene) + Na in liquid NH3, EtOH
B. Benzoic acid + Na in liquid NH3, EtOH
C. Toluene + Na in liquid NH3, EtOH
D. Naphthalene + Na in liquid NH3, EtOH at -33°C
List II:
I. 1-Methylcyclohexa-1,4-diene (alkyl EDG resides on an sp2 carbon)
II. 1-Methoxycyclohexa-1,4-diene (EDG resides on an sp2 carbon)
III. 1,4-Dihydronaphthalene (reduction confined to one ring preserving a stable 6-pi benzene ring)
IV. Cyclohexa-1,5-diene-1-carboxylic acid (EWG resides on an sp3 carbon)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Anisole (Methoxybenzene) + Na in liquid NH3, EtOH): The methoxy group donates electron density through resonance; electron addition occurs to form radical anions with charge localized at ortho and meta positions, directing protonation to ipso/meta positions. Therefore, A corresponds to II.
Step 2: Match item B (Benzoic acid + Na in liquid NH3, EtOH): The carboxylate group is electron-withdrawing; radical-anion electron density is highest at the ipso and para positions, directing protonation such that the -COOH group ends up on an sp3 carbon. Therefore, B corresponds to IV.
Step 3: Match item C (Toluene + Na in liquid NH3, EtOH): The electron-donating methyl group directs protonation away from the substituted position initially, preserving the methyl group on an unconjugated 1,4-diene sp2 carbon. Therefore, C corresponds to I.
Step 4: Match item D (Naphthalene + Na in liquid NH3, EtOH at -33°C): Reduction occurs preferentially in one ring across the 1,4-positions; the remaining benzene ring retains its 36 kcal/mol aromatic resonance stabilization. Therefore, D corresponds to III.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III, which corresponds to Option C.

subject: Chemistry
questionText:
Match the strained or bicyclic alkene additions in List I with their rearrangement pathways and products in List II:
List I:
A. Methylenecyclobutane + H3O+ (aqueous acid)
B. alpha-Pinene + dry HCl gas
C. Norbornene + HBr
D. 1-Methylcyclopentene + HBr (cold, dry)
List II:
I. Bornyl chloride formed via Wagner-Meerwein bicyclic skeletal rearrangement
II. 1-Bromo-1-methylcyclopentane formed without ring rearrangement via stable 3° cation
III. 1-Methylcyclobutanol and Cyclopentanol formed via ring expansion of cyclobutylcarbinyl cation
IV. exo-2-Bromonorbornane formed predominantly via non-classical 2-norbornyl carbocation
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Methylenecyclobutane + H3O+ (aqueous acid)): Protonation gives a cyclobutylcarbinyl carbocation that undergoes rapid Wagner-Meerwein ring expansion to the cyclopentyl cation, driven by relief of ~26 kcal/mol of ring strain. Therefore, A corresponds to III.
Step 2: Match item B (alpha-Pinene + dry HCl gas): Protonation of the endocyclic double bond of pinene creates a carbocation that undergoes deep skeletal migration of the cyclobutane bridge to relieve 4-membered ring strain, forming bornyl chloride. Therefore, B corresponds to I.
Step 3: Match item C (Norbornene + HBr): Protonation yields the bridged non-classical norbornyl cation; nucleophilic attack of bromide occurs stereospecifically from the less hindered exo face. Therefore, C corresponds to IV.
Step 4: Match item D (1-Methylcyclopentene + HBr (cold, dry)): Protonation generates a tertiary cyclopentyl carbocation directly; because the 5-membered ring is largely strain-free, it undergoes direct bromide capture without skeletal rearrangement. Therefore, D corresponds to II.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II, which corresponds to Option D.

subject: Chemistry
questionText:
Match the polycyclic aromatic substitutions in List I with their mechanistic control and orientation in List II:
List I:
A. Naphthalene + conc. H2SO4 at 353 K (80°C)
B. Naphthalene + conc. H2SO4 at 433 K (160°C)
C. Anthracene + Br2 in CS2 at 273 K
D. Phenanthrene + Br2 in CCl4 at room temperature
List II:
I. 9,10-Dibromoanthracene formed by attack at C-9 and C-10 positions
II. Naphthalene-2-sulfonic acid formed under thermodynamic control (beta-substitution)
III. 9,10-Dibromo-9,10-dihydrophenanthrene formed by electrophilic addition across C9-C10
IV. Naphthalene-1-sulfonic acid formed under kinetic control (alpha-substitution)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Naphthalene + conc. H2SO4 at 353 K (80°C)): Attack at the alpha (C-1) position proceeds through an arenium intermediate having two resonance structures that preserve the intact benzene ring, yielding a lower activation energy than beta-attack. Therefore, A corresponds to IV.
Step 2: Match item B (Naphthalene + conc. H2SO4 at 433 K (160°C)): At high temperature, sulfonation is reversible; the alpha-isomer suffers steric peri-interaction with the C-8 hydrogen, so equilibrium shifts to the less strained beta-isomer. Therefore, B corresponds to II.
Step 3: Match item C (Anthracene + Br2 in CS2 at 273 K): Electrophilic substitution at the central 9,10-positions leaves two fully aromatic, isolated 6-pi benzene rings intact (retaining 72 kcal/mol aromatic resonance energy). Therefore, C corresponds to I.
Step 4: Match item D (Phenanthrene + Br2 in CCl4 at room temperature): The C9-C10 bond in phenanthrene has significant localized double-bond character (bond length 1.35 A); addition across this bond preserves two biphenyl-like aromatic sextets. Therefore, D corresponds to III.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III, which corresponds to Option A.

subject: Chemistry
questionText:
Match the halogenated substrates and elimination conditions in List I with their mechanistic pathway and product distribution in List II:
List I:
A. 2-Bromopentane + NaOEt in EtOH at 350 K
B. 2-Bromopentane + Potassium tert-butoxide (t-BuOK) in t-BuOH
C. 2-Fluoropentane + NaOEt in EtOH
D. DDT + ethanolic KOH heated
List II:
I. Pent-1-ene is the major product formed via an E2 mechanism with Hofmann orientation
II. 1,1-Dichloro-2,2-bis(p-chlorophenyl)ethene (DDE) formed via an E1cB elimination
III. trans-Pent-2-ene is the major product formed via an E2 mechanism with Zaitsev orientation
IV. Pent-1-ene is the major product formed via an E1cB-like transition state
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (2-Bromopentane + NaOEt in EtOH at 350 K): A small, unhindered strong base abstracts a beta-proton from the more substituted carbon via an anti-periplanar transition state, yielding the thermodynamically more stable trans-alkene. Therefore, A corresponds to III.
Step 2: Match item B (2-Bromopentane + Potassium tert-butoxide (t-BuOK) in t-BuOH): The bulky tert-butoxide base cannot easily access the sterically shielded internal secondary beta-hydrogens, selectively deprotonating the more accessible primary methyl hydrogens. Therefore, B corresponds to I.
Step 3: Match item C (2-Fluoropentane + NaOEt in EtOH): Fluoride is a very poor leaving group with strong -I effect, making the beta-hydrogens acidic; the transition state develops extensive carbanion character, favoring the less substituted, more stable primary carbanion. Therefore, C corresponds to IV.
Step 4: Match item D (DDT + ethanolic KOH heated): The benzylic proton is strongly acidified by two chlorophenyl rings; base deprotonates to form a stable carbanion, which then expels a chloride ion from the adjacent trichloromethyl carbon. Therefore, D corresponds to II.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II, which corresponds to Option B.

subject: Chemistry
questionText:
Match the conjugated diene additions and cycloadditions in List I with their mechanistic governing rules in List II:
List I:
A. Buta-1,3-diene + HBr at 193 K (-80°C)
B. Buta-1,3-diene + HBr at 313 K (+40°C)
C. Cyclopentadiene + Maleic anhydride at 298 K
D. Buta-1,3-diene + Ethyne heated
List II:
I. endo-Bicyclo[2.2.1]hept-5-ene-2,3-dicarboxylic anhydride formed via endo-rule
II. 3-Bromobut-1-ene formed as major product under kinetic control (1,2-addition)
III. Cyclohexa-1,4-diene formed via thermal [4+2] Diels-Alder cycloaddition
IV. 1-Bromobut-2-ene formed as major product under thermodynamic control (1,4-addition)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Buta-1,3-diene + HBr at 193 K (-80°C)): At low temperature, the reaction is irreversible and controlled by the rate of product formation; the 1,2-product forms faster because bromide attacks the adjacent carbon (proximity effect) in the ion pair. Therefore, A corresponds to II.
Step 2: Match item B (Buta-1,3-diene + HBr at 313 K (+40°C)): At higher temperature, the addition is reversible; the system equilibrates to the most stable product, which is the internal, more substituted disubstituted alkene (1,4-adduct). Therefore, B corresponds to IV.
Step 3: Match item C (Cyclopentadiene + Maleic anhydride at 298 K): In the Diels-Alder [4+2] cycloaddition, secondary orbital overlap between the carbonyl pi-orbitals of maleic anhydride and the diene pi-system stabilizes the endo transition state over exo. Therefore, C corresponds to I.
Step 4: Match item D (Buta-1,3-diene + Ethyne heated): Concerted suprafacial [4pi_s + 2pi_s] cycloaddition of a conjugated diene in s-cis conformation with an alkyne dienophile generates an unconjugated six-membered cyclic diene. Therefore, D corresponds to III.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III, which corresponds to Option C.

subject: Chemistry
questionText:
Match the hydrocarbon oxidative degradations in List I with their stoichiometric cleavage products in List II:
List I:
A. Toluene + alkaline KMnO4 heated, then acidified
B. tert-Butylbenzene + alkaline KMnO4 heated, then acidified
C. o-Xylene + (i) O3, (ii) Zn / H2O
D. Benzene + V2O5 / O2 at 773 K
List II:
I. No reaction; substrate remains completely unaffected by oxidation
II. Maleic anhydride formed by catalytic ring cleavage and air oxidation
III. Benzoic acid (C6H5COOH) formed by complete benzylic oxidation
IV. Glyoxal, Methylglyoxal, and Dimethylglyoxal in 3:2:1 molar ratio
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Toluene + alkaline KMnO4 heated, then acidified): The presence of benzylic C-H bonds allows free radical/oxidative attack by permanganate, degrading the alkyl side chain completely to a carboxyl group. Therefore, A corresponds to III.
Step 2: Match item B (tert-Butylbenzene + alkaline KMnO4 heated, then acidified): tert-Butylbenzene lacks benzylic hydrogen atoms (the benzylic carbon is quaternary); without benzylic C-H bonds, permanganate cannot initiate oxidation. Therefore, B corresponds to I.
Step 3: Match item C (o-Xylene + (i) O3, (ii) Zn / H2O): Because benzene oscillates between two Kekule structures in 1:1 ratio, ozonolysis cleaves alternating double bonds, yielding three dialdehydes in a precise 3:2:1 ratio, confirming aromatic resonance. Therefore, C corresponds to IV.
Step 4: Match item D (Benzene + V2O5 / O2 at 773 K): Under drastic heterogeneous catalytic conditions at 500°C over vanadium pentoxide, two carbons of benzene are lost as CO2 and water, while four carbons are oxidized into maleic anhydride. Therefore, D corresponds to II.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II, which corresponds to Option D.

subject: Chemistry
questionText:
Match the named preparation methods for organic halides in List I with their reagents and driving principles in List II:
List I:
A. Finkelstein reaction
B. Swarts reaction
C. Darzens process
D. Hunsdiecker reaction
List II:
I. Alcohol + SOCl2 in pyridine yielding pure alkyl chloride with gaseous byproducts (SO2 and HCl)
II. Alkyl chloride/bromide heated with heavy metal fluorides (AgF, Hg2F2, CoF2, SbF3) yielding alkyl fluoride
III. Silver carboxylate (RCOOAg) + Br2 in refluxing CCl4 yielding alkyl bromide with loss of CO2
IV. Alkyl chloride/bromide + NaI in dry acetone yielding alkyl iodide via precipitation of NaCl/NaBr
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Finkelstein reaction): Sodium iodide is soluble in dry acetone, whereas NaCl and NaBr are insoluble and precipitate out, driving the equilibrium forward according to Le Chatelier's principle. Therefore, A corresponds to IV.
Step 2: Match item B (Swarts reaction): Fluorination of alkyl halides is best achieved by heating with metallic fluorides, which exchange halogen to provide pure fluoroalkanes. Therefore, B corresponds to II.
Step 3: Match item C (Darzens process): Thionyl chloride reacts cleanly with alcohols; the byproducts SO2 and HCl escape as gases, driving completion and leaving the pure alkyl chloride. Therefore, C corresponds to I.
Step 4: Match item D (Hunsdiecker reaction): Thermal decarboxylation of silver carboxylates in the presence of bromine proceeds via free radicals to give an alkyl bromide containing one less carbon atom. Therefore, D corresponds to III.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III, which corresponds to Option A.

subject: Chemistry
questionText:
Match the nucleophilic substitution mechanisms (SN1 vs SN2) in List I with their defining mechanistic and stereochemical characteristics in List II:
List I:
A. SN1 Reaction Kinetics
B. SN2 Reaction Kinetics
C. SN1 Stereochemical Outcome
D. SN2 Stereochemical Outcome
List II:
I. Second-order kinetics; rate = k[R-X][Nu-], dependent on both substrate and nucleophile
II. Complete stereochemical inversion of configuration (Walden inversion) via backside attack
III. First-order kinetics; rate = k[R-X], independent of nucleophile concentration and strength
IV. Racemization (formation of both enantiomers, often with slight excess of inversion due to ion pairing)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (SN1 Reaction Kinetics): The rate-determining step is the unimolecular heterolytic dissociation of the carbon-halogen bond to generate a carbocation intermediate. Therefore, A corresponds to III.
Step 2: Match item B (SN2 Reaction Kinetics): The reaction occurs in a single concerted step where nucleophilic attack and leaving group departure take place simultaneously via a pentacoordinate transition state. Therefore, B corresponds to I.
Step 3: Match item C (SN1 Stereochemical Outcome): The carbocation intermediate has a planar sp2 geometry; nucleophilic attack from the top face or bottom face occurs with comparable probability. Therefore, C corresponds to IV.
Step 4: Match item D (SN2 Stereochemical Outcome): The nucleophile approaches the electrophilic carbon from 180° opposite the leaving group, causing an umbrella-like inversion of the three remaining substituents. Therefore, D corresponds to II.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II, which corresponds to Option B.

subject: Chemistry
questionText:
Match the polyhalogen compounds in List I with their characteristic properties and practical applications in List II:
List I:
A. Chloroform (CHCl3) on exposure to light and air
B. Iodoform (CHI3)
C. Carbon tetrachloride (CCl4)
D. DDT [p,p'-Dichlorodiphenyltrichloroethane]
List II:
I. Non-flammable dense solvent formerly used under the name 'Pyrene' in fire extinguishers
II. Slowly oxidized to poisonous Carbonyl chloride (Phosgene, COCl2); prevented by storing in dark bottles with 1% ethanol
III. Persistent non-biodegradable organochlorine insecticide that bioaccumulates through food chains
IV. Bright yellow crystalline solid with pungent odor, historically used as an antiseptic due to liberation of free iodine
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Chloroform (CHCl3) on exposure to light and air): Light-induced free radical oxidation produces toxic phosgene; added ethanol reacts with any trace phosgene formed to convert it into harmless diethyl carbonate. Therefore, A corresponds to II.
Step 2: Match item B (Iodoform (CHI3)): Iodoform was widely used in medicine because it gradually decomposes in contact with skin tissues to release free iodine, which acts as the active antiseptic agent. Therefore, B corresponds to IV.
Step 3: Match item C (Carbon tetrachloride (CCl4)): CCl4 vapors are dense and non-combustible, settling over flames to displace oxygen; however, at high temperatures it can generate toxic phosgene, limiting modern use. Therefore, C corresponds to I.
Step 4: Match item D (DDT [p,p'-Dichlorodiphenyltrichloroethane]): DDT is highly lipid-soluble and resistant to environmental degradation, leading to severe bioaccumulation in fatty tissues of wildlife and eggshell thinning in birds. Therefore, D corresponds to III.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III, which corresponds to Option C.

subject: Chemistry
questionText:
Match the haloalkane reactions with ambident nucleophiles in List I with their primary organic products in List II:
List I:
A. Alkyl halide (R-X) + KCN in aqueous ethanol
B. Alkyl halide (R-X) + AgCN in aqueous ethanol
C. Alkyl halide (R-X) + KNO2 in aqueous ethanol
D. Alkyl halide (R-X) + AgNO2 in aqueous ethanol
List II:
I. Alkyl isocyanide / Carbylamine (R-NC) formed as major product
II. Nitroalkane (R-NO2) formed as major product
III. Alkyl cyanide / Alkane nitrile (R-CN) formed as major product
IV. Alkyl nitrite (R-O-N=O) formed as major product
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Alkyl halide (R-X) + KCN in aqueous ethanol): Potassium cyanide is ionic ([K+] [:C#N:-]); the carbon atom has higher nucleophilicity and forms a stronger C-C bond than the C-N bond, making R-CN the major product. Therefore, A corresponds to III.
Step 2: Match item B (Alkyl halide (R-X) + AgCN in aqueous ethanol): Silver cyanide is largely covalent (Ag-C#N:); the carbon atom is bonded to silver, leaving the unshared electron pair on nitrogen to attack the alkyl group. Therefore, B corresponds to I.
Step 3: Match item C (Alkyl halide (R-X) + KNO2 in aqueous ethanol): Potassium nitrite is ionic (K+ [O-N=O]-); the negative charge is concentrated on oxygen, which attacks the alkyl group preferentially to form an alkyl nitrite. Therefore, C corresponds to IV.
Step 4: Match item D (Alkyl halide (R-X) + AgNO2 in aqueous ethanol): Silver nitrite has significant covalent Ag-O character, leaving the lone pair of electrons on the nitrogen atom free to perform nucleophilic attack on the carbon atom. Therefore, D corresponds to II.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II, which corresponds to Option D.

subject: Chemistry
questionText:
Match the alkyl halides in List I with their relative reactivity in SN1 and SN2 substitutions in List II:
List I:
A. Neopentyl bromide [(CH3)3C-CH2Br]
B. Allyl bromide (CH2=CH-CH2Br)
C. Benzyl chloride (C6H5CH2Cl)
D. 1-Bromobutane vs 2-Bromobutane in SN2 with NaI
List II:
I. Highly reactive in both SN1 (benzylic carbocation resonance) and SN2 (phenyl conjugation in TS)
II. Exceptionally reactive in both SN1 (resonance-stabilized allylic cation) and SN2 (pi-orbital overlap with TS)
III. 1-Bromobutane reacts substantially faster than 2-bromobutane due to lower steric hindrance at 1° carbon
IV. Extremely unreactive in SN2 (reacts ~10^-5 times slower than ethyl bromide) due to severe steric crowding by beta-methyl groups
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Neopentyl bromide [(CH3)3C-CH2Br]): Even though the bromide is attached to a primary carbon, the bulky tert-butyl group on the adjacent beta-carbon blocks backside nucleophilic approach to the sigma* orbital. Therefore, A corresponds to IV.
Step 2: Match item B (Allyl bromide (CH2=CH-CH2Br)): In SN1, heterolysis gives an allylic carbocation with charge delocalized over 3 carbons; in SN2, the adjacent pi-bond provides orbital conjugation that stabilizes the pentacoordinate TS. Therefore, B corresponds to II.
Step 3: Match item C (Benzyl chloride (C6H5CH2Cl)): Benzylic carbocation enjoys resonance over 4 canonical forms; similarly in SN2, the aromatic pi-electron cloud conjugates with the developing p-orbital in the transition state. Therefore, C corresponds to I.
Step 4: Match item D (1-Bromobutane vs 2-Bromobutane in SN2 with NaI): Primary alkyl halides offer far less steric barrier to backside nucleophilic approach than secondary alkyl halides, resulting in a significantly lower activation energy. Therefore, D corresponds to III.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III, which corresponds to Option A.

subject: Chemistry
questionText:
Match the chiral haloalkane substitutions in List I with their stereochemical outcome and mechanistic pathway in List II:
List I:
A. (R)-2-Bromooctane + NaOH in aqueous acetone
B. (R)-3-Chloro-3-methylhexane solvolysis in 80% aqueous acetone
C. (R)-Butan-2-ol + SOCl2 in dry ether
D. (R)-Butan-2-ol + SOCl2 in the presence of Pyridine
List II:
I. Racemic mixture (with slight excess of inversion) of (R) and (S) alcohols via SN1
II. (S)-2-Chlorobutane formed with inversion of configuration via an SN2 displacement
III. (S)-Octan-2-ol formed with 100% stereochemical inversion via concerted bimolecular SN2
IV. (R)-2-Chlorobutane formed with retention of configuration via internal nucleophilic substitution (SNi)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A ((R)-2-Bromooctane + NaOH in aqueous acetone): Hydroxide attacks exclusively from the backside opposite the departing bromide ion, resulting in an umbrella inversion that flips (R) to (S) configuration cleanly. Therefore, A corresponds to III.
Step 2: Match item B ((R)-3-Chloro-3-methylhexane solvolysis in 80% aqueous acetone): Ionization forms a planar 3° carbocation; frontside attack is slightly hindered by the departing chloride leaving group (intimate ion pair), leading to predominant racemization with minor net inversion. Therefore, B corresponds to I.
Step 3: Match item C ((R)-Butan-2-ol + SOCl2 in dry ether): Reaction forms an alkyl chlorosulfite ester intermediate; decomposition occurs through a concerted 4-membered cyclic transition state where chlorine attacks from the same front face. Therefore, C corresponds to IV.
Step 4: Match item D ((R)-Butan-2-ol + SOCl2 in the presence of Pyridine): Pyridine reacts with HCl to form pyridinium chloride; the free nucleophilic chloride ion attacks the chlorosulfite intermediate from the backside, causing complete Walden inversion. Therefore, D corresponds to II.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II, which corresponds to Option B.

subject: Chemistry
questionText:
Match the haloalkanes and elimination conditions in List I with the predominant alkene product and regiochemical rationale in List II:
List I:
A. 2-Bromobutane + ethanolic KOH heated
B. 2-Bromobutane + Potassium tert-butoxide (t-BuOK) in t-BuOH
C. 2-Fluorobutane + sodium ethoxide in ethanol
D. sec-Butyltrimethylammonium hydroxide heated (pyrolysis)
List II:
I. But-1-ene (major, ~70%) formed following Hofmann's rule due to poor leaving group ability
II. But-2-ene (major, ~80%) formed following Zaitsev's rule via E2 elimination
III. But-1-ene (major, ~95%) formed via classic Hofmann elimination of quaternary ammonium salt
IV. But-1-ene (major, ~70%) formed following Hofmann's rule due to base steric hindrance
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (2-Bromobutane + ethanolic KOH heated): A small strong base removes a proton from the more substituted beta-carbon, forming the more substituted, thermodynamically stable alkene (predominantly trans-but-2-ene). Therefore, A corresponds to II.
Step 2: Match item B (2-Bromobutane + Potassium tert-butoxide (t-BuOK) in t-BuOH): The bulky tert-butoxide ion encounters steric clash when approaching the secondary beta-hydrogens, selectively abstracting the sterically accessible primary beta-hydrogens. Therefore, B corresponds to IV.
Step 3: Match item C (2-Fluorobutane + sodium ethoxide in ethanol): Fluorine is a poor leaving group with a powerful -I effect; significant negative charge develops on the beta-carbon in the transition state (E1cB-like), favoring the less substituted carbanion. Therefore, C corresponds to I.
Step 4: Match item D (sec-Butyltrimethylammonium hydroxide heated (pyrolysis)): The bulky positively charged -N+(CH3)3 leaving group causes steric repulsion and exerts strong electron withdrawal, directing deprotonation strictly to the less hindered primary carbon. Therefore, D corresponds to III.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III, which corresponds to Option C.

subject: Chemistry
questionText:
Match the Grignard reagent (RMgX) reactions in List I with the resulting organic products in List II:
List I:
A. Methylmagnesium bromide + Ethanol (CH3CH2OH)
B. Methylmagnesium bromide + Solid Carbon dioxide (dry ice) followed by H3O+
C. Methylmagnesium bromide + Ethylene oxide (Oxirane) followed by H3O+
D. Methylmagnesium bromide + Propan-2-one (Acetone) followed by H3O+
List II:
I. Ethanoic acid (Acetic acid, CH3COOH) formed by nucleophilic addition to CO2
II. 2-Methylpropan-2-ol (tert-Butanol) formed by nucleophilic addition to the carbonyl group
III. Methane (CH4) gas formed via acid-base proton transfer from the acidic -OH group
IV. Propan-1-ol (CH3CH2CH2OH) formed via nucleophilic ring-opening of the strained epoxide
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Methylmagnesium bromide + Ethanol (CH3CH2OH)): Grignard reagents are powerful Bronsted bases (carbanions); they immediately deprotonate active-hydrogen compounds to form alkanes quantitatively (Zerewitinoff determination). Therefore, A corresponds to III.
Step 2: Match item B (Methylmagnesium bromide + Solid Carbon dioxide (dry ice) followed by H3O+): The carbanionic methyl group attacks the electrophilic carbon of carbon dioxide, forming a magnesium carboxylate salt that yields acetic acid upon acidic hydrolysis. Therefore, B corresponds to I.
Step 3: Match item C (Methylmagnesium bromide + Ethylene oxide (Oxirane) followed by H3O+): Nucleophilic attack on the less hindered carbon of the strained oxirane ring causes ring-opening, elongating the carbon chain by two carbons to yield a primary alcohol. Therefore, C corresponds to IV.
Step 4: Match item D (Methylmagnesium bromide + Propan-2-one (Acetone) followed by H3O+): Addition of methyl carbanion to the electrophilic carbonyl carbon of acetone generates a tertiary alkoxide, which is protonated by aqueous acid to give a tertiary alcohol. Therefore, D corresponds to II.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II, which corresponds to Option D.

subject: Chemistry
questionText:
Match the substituted haloarenes in List I with the required conditions for nucleophilic aromatic substitution (SNAr) in List II:
List I:
A. 2,4,6-Trinitrochlorobenzene (Picryl chloride)
B. 2,4-Dinitrochlorobenzene
C. 4-Nitrochlorobenzene
D. Chlorobenzene (unsubstituted)
List II:
I. Requires heating with aqueous NaOH at 443 K (170°C) followed by acidification
II. Hydrolyzes to 2,4-Dinitrophenol on heating with aqueous Na2CO3 at 370 K
III. Requires drastic industrial conditions (aqueous NaOH at 623 K and 300 atm, Dow's process)
IV. Hydrolyzes rapidly to Picric acid merely on warming with warm water at 323 K (50°C)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (2,4,6-Trinitrochlorobenzene (Picryl chloride)): Three nitro groups situated ortho and para to the chlorine strongly stabilize the Meisenheimer intermediate through extensive resonance delocalization of the negative charge onto all oxygen atoms. Therefore, A corresponds to IV.
Step 2: Match item B (2,4-Dinitrochlorobenzene): Two ortho/para nitro groups sufficiently lower the activation energy of nucleophilic addition, allowing replacement of chlorine using weak base under mild heating. Therefore, B corresponds to II.
Step 3: Match item C (4-Nitrochlorobenzene): A single para-nitro group activates the ring moderately; harsher heating with strong sodium hydroxide is required to displace the chloride ion. Therefore, C corresponds to I.
Step 4: Match item D (Chlorobenzene (unsubstituted)): Unactivated haloarenes are extremely resistant to SNAr due to partial double-bond character of C-Cl bond, sp2 hybridization of carbon, and lack of resonance stabilization in intermediate. Therefore, D corresponds to III.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III, which corresponds to Option A.

subject: Chemistry
questionText:
Match the leaving groups in List I with their relative leaving ability in nucleophilic substitutions in List II:
List I:
A. Trifluoromethanesulfonate (Triflate, CF3SO3-)
B. p-Toluenesulfonate (Tosylate, TsO-)
C. Iodide ion (I-)
D. Fluoride ion (F-)
List II:
I. Excellent leaving group; departs ~10^4 times faster than bromide in SN2 displacements
II. Poorest leaving group in aliphatic nucleophilic substitutions (essentially unreactive in SN2)
III. Super leaving group; departs ~10^6 times faster than tosylate due to intense -I effect of CF3
IV. Best leaving group among halides (relative rate: I- > Br- > Cl- >> F-)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Trifluoromethanesulfonate (Triflate, CF3SO3-)): The conjugate base of triflic acid is extraordinarily stable because the negative charge is delocalized over 3 sulfonate oxygens and inductively withdrawn by 3 fluorine atoms. Therefore, A corresponds to III.
Step 2: Match item B (p-Toluenesulfonate (Tosylate, TsO-)): Resonance stabilization of the sulfonate anion across three equivalent oxygen atoms makes tosylate a very weak base and an exceptional leaving group. Therefore, B corresponds to I.
Step 3: Match item C (Iodide ion (I-)): Iodide has the largest ionic radius, lowest basicity, and forms the weakest carbon-halogen bond (~213 kJ/mol), making C-I cleavage easiest. Therefore, C corresponds to IV.
Step 4: Match item D (Fluoride ion (F-)): Fluoride is the strongest base among halide ions and forms a very short, immensely strong C-F bond (~485 kJ/mol), presenting a huge kinetic barrier to heterolysis. Therefore, D corresponds to II.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II, which corresponds to Option B.

subject: Chemistry
questionText:
Match the solvent and medium conditions in List I with their effect on nucleophilicity and substitution rates in List II:
List I:
A. Halide nucleophilicity in Polar Protic Solvents (H2O, MeOH)
B. Halide nucleophilicity in Polar Aprotic Solvents (DMF, DMSO, Acetone)
C. Addition of 18-Crown-6 to Potassium fluoride in Benzene
D. Solvolysis of tert-butyl chloride in 80% Water / 20% Ethanol vs 100% Ethanol
List II:
I. Solubilizes KF in non-polar benzene, creating 'naked' fluoride with super-nucleophilic reactivity
II. I- > Br- > Cl- > F- (reversal of basicity order due to strong hydrogen-bonding hydration)
III. Rate accelerates by ~10^4 in water-rich solvent due to superior stabilization of the polar transition state
IV. F- > Cl- > Br- > I- (parallel to basicity order because anions remain desolvated and 'naked')
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Halide nucleophilicity in Polar Protic Solvents (H2O, MeOH)): Small anions with concentrated charge (like F-) are tightly caged by a shell of hydrogen-bonded protic solvent molecules; larger, polarizable I- is weakly solvated and attacks freely. Therefore, A corresponds to II.
Step 2: Match item B (Halide nucleophilicity in Polar Aprotic Solvents (DMF, DMSO, Acetone)): Polar aprotic solvents solvate cations via dipole-dipole interactions but leave anions poorly solvated; the smaller fluoride ion retains high charge density and becomes the most nucleophilic. Therefore, B corresponds to IV.
Step 3: Match item C (Addition of 18-Crown-6 to Potassium fluoride in Benzene): The cyclic crown ether specifically chelates the potassium cation (K+) inside its cavity, releasing unsolvated, highly reactive fluoride ions into the organic phase. Therefore, C corresponds to I.
Step 4: Match item D (Solvolysis of tert-butyl chloride in 80% Water / 20% Ethanol vs 100% Ethanol): The SN1 rate-determining transition state develops large partial positive and negative charges; a more polar, hydrogen-bonding solvent stabilizes this polarized TS, lowering activation energy. Therefore, D corresponds to III.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III, which corresponds to Option C.

subject: Chemistry
questionText:
Match the chloroform reactions in List I with their mechanistic pathway and functional products in List II:
List I:
A. Chloroform + aq. KOH with Phenol (Reimer-Tiemann reaction)
B. Primary amine + CHCl3 + alc. KOH (Carbylamine reaction)
C. Chloroform + Propan-2-one (Acetone) in presence of solid KOH
D. Chloroform + conc. HNO3 heated
List II:
I. Alkyl isocyanide / Carbylamine (R-NC) with extremely foul odor (specific test for 1° amines)
II. Chloropicrin (CCl3NO2, nitrochloroform), a powerful tear gas and fumigant
III. Salicylaldehyde (2-hydroxybenzaldehyde) formed via electrophilic attack of dichlorocarbene (:CCl2)
IV. Chloretone [1,1,1-trichloro-2-methylpropan-2-ol] formed by nucleophilic addition to carbonyl
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Chloroform + aq. KOH with Phenol (Reimer-Tiemann reaction)): Strong base deprotonates chloroform to form trichloromethyl carbanion, which loses Cl- to generate neutral electrophilic dichlorocarbene (:CCl2) that attacks phenoxide at the ortho position. Therefore, A corresponds to III.
Step 2: Match item B (Primary amine + CHCl3 + alc. KOH (Carbylamine reaction)): Dichlorocarbene adds to the primary amine nitrogen; subsequent alpha-eliminations generate a triple bond between carbon and nitrogen, yielding the characteristic repulsive smelling isocyanide. Therefore, B corresponds to I.
Step 3: Match item C (Chloroform + Propan-2-one (Acetone) in presence of solid KOH): Deprotonation by solid KOH yields trichloromethyl carbanion (:CCl3-), which adds to the electrophilic carbonyl group of acetone to give chloretone, used as a hypnotic. Therefore, C corresponds to IV.
Step 4: Match item D (Chloroform + conc. HNO3 heated): Electrophilic nitration of chloroform by concentrated nitric acid replaces the acidic C-H hydrogen with a nitro group to give chloropicrin. Therefore, D corresponds to II.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II, which corresponds to Option D.

subject: Chemistry
questionText:
Match the cyclohexyl halide stereoisomers in List I with their E2 elimination behavior in List II:
List I:
A. Neomenthyl chloride + NaOEt in EtOH
B. Menthyl chloride + NaOEt in EtOH
C. trans-1-Bromo-2-methylcyclohexane + NaOEt in EtOH
D. cis-1-Bromo-2-methylcyclohexane + NaOEt in EtOH
List II:
I. Yields 3-methylcyclohexene as major product because anti-periplanar beta-H exists only at C-6
II. Reacts slowly to give 2-menthene exclusively (~100%) as the anti-Zaitsev product
III. Yields 1-methylcyclohexene (Zaitsev product) rapidly because axial beta-H is available at C-2
IV. Reacts rapidly (~40 times faster than menthyl chloride) to give 3-menthene as major Zaitsev product
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Neomenthyl chloride + NaOEt in EtOH): In neomenthyl chloride, the chlorine atom occupies an axial position in the more stable chair conformer, having anti-periplanar hydrogens at both C-2 and C-4, enabling rapid Zaitsev elimination. Therefore, A corresponds to IV.
Step 2: Match item B (Menthyl chloride + NaOEt in EtOH): Chlorine is equatorial in the stable chair; to eliminate, it must flip to the less stable chair (all 3 groups axial). In that conformer, only the axial H at C-2 is anti-periplanar (C-4 has an isopropyl group). Therefore, B corresponds to II.
Step 3: Match item C (trans-1-Bromo-2-methylcyclohexane + NaOEt in EtOH): When bromine is axial, the trans-methyl group is equatorial; anti-coplanar coplanar relationship is impossible with the C-2 proton, directing elimination exclusively toward C-6. Therefore, C corresponds to I.
Step 4: Match item D (cis-1-Bromo-2-methylcyclohexane + NaOEt in EtOH): In the chair conformer with axial bromine, the cis-methyl is equatorial, allowing the axial hydrogen at C-2 to assume an anti-periplanar geometry with Br, yielding the more substituted alkene. Therefore, D corresponds to III.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III, which corresponds to Option A.

subject: Chemistry
questionText:
Match the substrates undergoing Neighbouring Group Participation (NGP / Anchimeric Assistance) in List I with their mechanistic outcome in List II:
List I:
A. 2-Chloroethyl ethyl sulfide (Mustard gas analog) solvolysis in water
B. Acetolysis of trans-2-iodocyclohexyl brosylate
C. Acetolysis of erythro-3-bromo-2-butanol
D. Solvolysis of exo-2-norbornyl brosylate vs endo-2-norbornyl brosylate
List II:
I. Yields exclusively trans-1,2-diacetoxycyclohexane with complete retention of configuration
II. exo-Isomer reacts 350 times faster than endo due to C1-C6 sigma-bond anchimeric assistance
III. Accelerates by ~10^4 relative to chloroalkanes via a cyclic episulfonium ion intermediate
IV. Yields meso-butane-2,3-diacetate via a symmetric bridged bromonium ion
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (2-Chloroethyl ethyl sulfide (Mustard gas analog) solvolysis in water): The sulfur lone pair performs an internal backside displacement (intramolecular SN2) to form a strained 3-membered episulfonium ion, which is rapidly captured by water. Therefore, A corresponds to III.
Step 2: Match item B (Acetolysis of trans-2-iodocyclohexyl brosylate): The trans-iodine atom acts as a neighboring group, attacking from the back to form a cyclic iodonium intermediate (first inversion); acetate then attacks the bridged ion (second inversion), giving net retention. Therefore, B corresponds to I.
Step 3: Match item C (Acetolysis of erythro-3-bromo-2-butanol): Participation of the neighboring bromine atom creates a symmetric bridged bromonium ion; nucleophilic attack by acetate at either carbon yields the meso stereoisomer. Therefore, C corresponds to IV.
Step 4: Match item D (Solvolysis of exo-2-norbornyl brosylate vs endo-2-norbornyl brosylate): In the exo isomer, the backside of the C-2 bond is perfectly aligned with the C1-C6 sigma bonding electrons, assisting leaving group departure to form the bridged non-classical carbocation directly. Therefore, D corresponds to II.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II, which corresponds to Option B.

subject: Chemistry
questionText:
Match the haloalkane solvolysis systems in List I with their deep carbocation rearrangement pathway in List II:
List I:
A. Solvolysis of 2-bromo-3,3-dimethylbutane in aqueous ethanol
B. Solvolysis of Neopentyl iodide [(CH3)3C-CH2I] with AgNO3
C. Solvolysis of (Cyclobutylmethyl) bromide in aqueous formic acid
D. Solvolysis of Pinacolyl chloride [(CH3)3C-CH(Cl)CH3] in water
List II:
I. Yields cyclopentanol and cyclopentene via ring expansion driven by release of 4-membered ring strain
II. Yields predominantly 2,3-dimethylbut-2-ene via 1,2-methide shift of 2° to 3° carbocation
III. Yields 2,3-dimethylbutan-2-ol as the major substitution product via 1,2-methyl migration
IV. Yields 2-methylbut-2-ene and tert-pentyl alcohol via concerted/instantaneous 1,2-methide shift
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Solvolysis of 2-bromo-3,3-dimethylbutane in aqueous ethanol): Ionization yields secondary cation (CH3)3C-CH(+)-CH3; instantaneous 1,2-methyl shift affords the tertiary cation (CH3)2C(+)-CH(CH3)2, which eliminates to the thermodynamic tetrasubstituted alkene. Therefore, A corresponds to II.
Step 2: Match item B (Solvolysis of Neopentyl iodide [(CH3)3C-CH2I] with AgNO3): Primary neopentyl cation cannot exist as a free intermediate; Ag+-assisted departure of iodide is concerted with 1,2-methyl migration to form the tertiary tert-pentyl carbocation. Therefore, B corresponds to IV.
Step 3: Match item C (Solvolysis of (Cyclobutylmethyl) bromide in aqueous formic acid): Ionization triggers Wagner-Meerwein ring expansion from a strained 4-membered cyclobutane ring (~26 kcal/mol strain) into a stable 5-membered cyclopentyl carbocation. Therefore, C corresponds to I.
Step 4: Match item D (Solvolysis of Pinacolyl chloride [(CH3)3C-CH(Cl)CH3] in water): Loss of chloride from the secondary carbon triggers a rapid 1,2-methide shift to generate the more stable tertiary carbocation before nucleophilic capture by water. Therefore, D corresponds to III.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III, which corresponds to Option C.

subject: Chemistry
questionText:
Match the multi-step Grignard and organometallic additions in List I with their final synthesized products in List II:
List I:
A. Ethyl formate (HCOOCH2CH3) + 2 moles of CH3MgBr followed by H3O+
B. Ethyl acetate (CH3COOCH2CH3) + 2 moles of CH3MgBr followed by H3O+
C. Diethyl carbonate [(EtO)2C=O] + 3 moles of CH3MgBr followed by H3O+
D. Acetyl chloride (CH3COCl) + 1 mole of Lithium dimethylcuprate [(CH3)2CuLi]
List II:
I. 2-Methylpropan-2-ol (tert-Butanol) formed via ketone intermediate and subsequent addition
II. Propan-2-one (Acetone) cleanly obtained without over-addition to tertiary alcohol
III. Propan-2-ol (secondary alcohol) formed via addition to formyl carbonyl and subsequent addition
IV. tert-Butanol (2-methylpropan-2-ol) formed by three consecutive additions with loss of two ethoxides
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Ethyl formate (HCOOCH2CH3) + 2 moles of CH3MgBr followed by H3O+): First mole of Grignard attacks the ester, eliminating ethoxide to generate acetaldehyde; the second mole adds to acetaldehyde to produce a secondary alcohol (isopropanol). Therefore, A corresponds to III.
Step 2: Match item B (Ethyl acetate (CH3COOCH2CH3) + 2 moles of CH3MgBr followed by H3O+): First mole attacks the acetate ester, expelling ethoxide to form acetone; the second mole of Grignard immediately adds to acetone to generate a tertiary alcohol. Therefore, B corresponds to I.
Step 3: Match item C (Diethyl carbonate [(EtO)2C=O] + 3 moles of CH3MgBr followed by H3O+): Sequential substitution of two ethoxy groups converts carbonate first to ethyl acetate, then to acetone, which finally adds the third methyl group to yield tert-butanol. Therefore, C corresponds to IV.
Step 4: Match item D (Acetyl chloride (CH3COCl) + 1 mole of Lithium dimethylcuprate [(CH3)2CuLi]): Gilman reagents are milder nucleophiles than Grignard reagents; they react cleanly with acid chlorides to give ketones, but do not add to ketones, preventing tertiary alcohol formation. Therefore, D corresponds to II.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II, which corresponds to Option D.

subject: Chemistry
questionText:
Match the unusual nucleophilic aromatic and aliphatic substitution phenomena in List I with their physical explanations in List II:
List I:
A. SNAr rate order: Ar-F >> Ar-Cl > Ar-Br > Ar-I (The Element Effect)
B. Phenacyl chloride (Ph-CO-CH2Cl) unusually high reactivity in SN2 (~10^5 times ethyl chloride)
C. Bridgehead 1-Bromoadamantane reactivity in SN1 solvolysis
D. 1-Bromobicyclo[2.2.1]heptane complete inertness to both SN1 and SN2
List II:
I. Undergoes SN1 solvolysis readily because the rigid cage pre-forms a pyramidal-flattened bridgehead cation
II. Stabilization of the SN2 pentacoordinate transition state by pi-conjugation with the adjacent carbonyl C=O LUMO
III. Cage geometry strictly prohibits backside attack for SN2 and violates Bredt's rule for planar SN1 carbocation
IV. Confirms nucleophilic attack (addition) is rate-determining; C-X cleavage occurs in a subsequent fast step
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (SNAr rate order: Ar-F >> Ar-Cl > Ar-Br > Ar-I (The Element Effect)): Fluorine has the greatest -I effect, strongly stabilizing the developing negative charge in the Meisenheimer intermediate; since C-X cleavage is not in the RDS, the high C-F bond strength does not impede rate. Therefore, A corresponds to IV.
Step 2: Match item B (Phenacyl chloride (Ph-CO-CH2Cl) unusually high reactivity in SN2 (~10^5 times ethyl chloride)): The p-orbital at the reacting carbon in the SN2 transition state overlaps with the adjacent pi* orbital of the carbonyl group, significantly delocalizing charge and lowering activation energy. Therefore, B corresponds to II.
Step 3: Match item C (Bridgehead 1-Bromoadamantane reactivity in SN1 solvolysis): Unlike smaller bicyclic systems, the adamantyl cage is large and flexible enough to accommodate the bridgehead carbocation without excessive angle strain. Therefore, C corresponds to I.
Step 4: Match item D (1-Bromobicyclo[2.2.1]heptane complete inertness to both SN1 and SN2): The small bicyclic [2.2.1] framework is completely rigid: backside nucleophilic approach is blocked by bridge carbons, and the bridgehead carbon cannot flatten into a 120° planar sp2 cation. Therefore, D corresponds to III.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III, which corresponds to Option A.

subject: Chemistry
questionText:
Match the unreactive or specialized organic halides in List I with their mechanistic justification in List II:
List I:
A. Vinyl chloride (CH2=CH-Cl)
B. Chlorobenzene (C6H5Cl)
C. 1-Bromobicyclo[2.2.2]octane inertness to SN2
D. Allyl chloride solvolysis rate compared to 1-chloropropane
List II:
I. Resistant to SN1 due to instability of phenyl cation and SN2 due to shielding by aromatic pi-cloud
II. Undergoes SN1 solvolysis ~10^6 times faster due to resonance stabilization of the allylic cation
III. Inert to SN1 and SN2 due to sp2 carbon hybridization, C-Cl partial double bond character, and pi repulsion
IV. Completely unreactive to SN2 because the cage interior completely blocks backside nucleophilic approach
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Vinyl chloride (CH2=CH-Cl)): The chlorine lone pair is conjugated with the double bond (CH2=CH-Cl <-> -CH2-CH=Cl+), shortening the C-Cl bond; backside attack on an sp2 carbon is sterically and electronically blocked. Therefore, A corresponds to III.
Step 2: Match item B (Chlorobenzene (C6H5Cl)): Heterolysis would form an sp-hybridized phenyl cation with positive charge in an sp2 hybrid orbital perpendicular to the pi-system, which is prohibitively high in energy. Therefore, B corresponds to I.
Step 3: Match item C (1-Bromobicyclo[2.2.2]octane inertness to SN2): The nucleophile must attack at 180° opposite the C-Br bond, but that vector points directly into the hollow interior of the locked hydrocarbon cage. Therefore, C corresponds to IV.
Step 4: Match item D (Allyl chloride solvolysis rate compared to 1-chloropropane): Departure of chloride produces an allylic carbocation [CH2=CH-CH2+ <-> +CH2-CH=CH2] where the empty p-orbital is fully conjugated across two equivalent resonance structures. Therefore, D corresponds to II.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II, which corresponds to Option B.

subject: Chemistry
questionText:
Match the haloform and alpha-halogenation mechanisms in List I with their kinetic and mechanistic features in List II:
List I:
A. Kinetics of base-promoted halogenation: Rate = k[Ketone][OH-]^1 [X2]^0
B. Acid-catalyzed halogenation of ketones (Monohalogenation dominance)
C. Base-catalyzed halogenation of methyl ketones (Trihalogenation runaway)
D. Cleavage of trihalomethyl ketone by hydroxide ion
List II:
I. Each successive halogen atom increases the acidity of remaining alpha-protons, accelerating subsequent halogenations
II. Zero-order in halogen; removal of alpha-proton by base (enolate formation) is the rate-determining step
III. Hydroxide adds to carbonyl carbon to form tetrahedral intermediate which expels the stabilized :CX3- leaving group
IV. Halogenation stops cleanly after one halogen atom because the electron-withdrawing halogen reduces carbonyl basicity
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Kinetics of base-promoted halogenation: Rate = k[Ketone][OH-]^1 [X2]^0): The rate is identical whether chlorine, bromine, or iodine is used, proving that the halogen does not participate in the rate-determining step, which is solely enolate ion generation. Therefore, A corresponds to II.
Step 2: Match item B (Acid-catalyzed halogenation of ketones (Monohalogenation dominance)): The introduced alpha-halogen exerts a strong -I effect, decreasing basicity of the carbonyl oxygen and slowing down the second protonation required to form the second enol. Therefore, B corresponds to IV.
Step 3: Match item C (Base-catalyzed halogenation of methyl ketones (Trihalogenation runaway)): The strong -I effect of halogen makes the remaining alpha-C-H bonds progressively more acidic, so the mono- and di-halo ketones are deprotonated faster than the initial ketone. Therefore, C corresponds to I.
Step 4: Match item D (Cleavage of trihalomethyl ketone by hydroxide ion): Addition of OH- produces a tetrahedral alkoxide; collapse of the C=O double bond expels the trihalomethyl carbanion (:CX3-), which is stabilized by three strongly electronegative halogens. Therefore, D corresponds to III.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III, which corresponds to Option C.

subject: Chemistry
questionText:
Match the substituted benzyne intermediates in List I with their regioselective nucleophilic addition products in List II:
List I:
A. 3-Methoxybenzyne + KNH2 in liquid NH3
B. 3-Methylbenzyne + KNH2 in liquid NH3
C. 1,2-Dibromobenzene treated with Lithium amalgam in dry ether
D. 1-Bromo-2-fluorobenzene treated with Magnesium in presence of Anthracene
List II:
I. ortho-Toluidine formed predominantly over meta-toluidine
II. Triptycene formed via [4+2] Diels-Alder cycloaddition across the 9,10-bridge of anthracene
III. meta-Anisidine (m-methoxyaniline) formed predominantly over ortho-anisidine
IV. Biphenylene formed via [2+2] dimerization of two generated benzyne molecules
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (3-Methoxybenzyne + KNH2 in liquid NH3): The methoxy group exerts a strong inductive electron-withdrawing (-I) effect; nucleophilic attack of NH2- occurs at the meta position so that the developing carbanionic negative charge resides at the ortho carbon adjacent to the -I group. Therefore, A corresponds to III.
Step 2: Match item B (3-Methylbenzyne + KNH2 in liquid NH3): The methyl group exerts an electron-donating (+I) inductive effect; negative charge developing ortho to the methyl group is destabilized, directing the carbanion to the meta carbon and the NH2 group to the ortho carbon. Therefore, B corresponds to I.
Step 3: Match item C (1,2-Dibromobenzene treated with Lithium amalgam in dry ether): Halogen-metal exchange followed by loss of LiBr generates benzyne in high concentration, which spontaneously dimerizes via formal [2+2] cycloaddition to form anti-aromatic-fused biphenylene. Therefore, C corresponds to IV.
Step 4: Match item D (1-Bromo-2-fluorobenzene treated with Magnesium in presence of Anthracene): Benzyne generated in situ acts as an exceptionally reactive dienophile, adding stereospecifically across the 9,10-positions of anthracene to yield the rigid paddlewheel-shaped triptycene. Therefore, D corresponds to II.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II, which corresponds to Option D.

subject: Chemistry
questionText:
Match the analytical tests for distinguishing 1°, 2°, and 3° alcohols in List I with their observable behavior and chemistry in List II:
List I:
A. Lucas reagent (conc. HCl + anhydrous ZnCl2) with 3° alcohol
B. Lucas reagent with 2° alcohol
C. Victor Meyer's test with 1° alcohol
D. Hot copper (Cu) catalyst at 573 K with 3° alcohol
List II:
I. Blood-red coloration upon treatment with HNO2 followed by alkali
II. Turbidity appears within 5 to 10 minutes at room temperature
III. Dehydration to an alkene (2-methylpropene from tert-butanol) instead of dehydrogenation
IV. Immediate appearance of turbidity/cloudiness at room temperature
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Lucas reagent (conc. HCl + anhydrous ZnCl2) with 3° alcohol): Tertiary alcohols undergo instantaneous SN1 reaction via stable 3° carbocations to form insoluble tertiary alkyl chlorides, giving immediate turbidity. Therefore, A corresponds to IV.
Step 2: Match item B (Lucas reagent with 2° alcohol): Secondary alcohols react at a moderate rate through 2° carbocations; cloudiness develops within several minutes upon standing at ambient temperature. Therefore, B corresponds to II.
Step 3: Match item C (Victor Meyer's test with 1° alcohol): Primary nitroalkane formed reacts with nitrous acid to yield nitrolic acid [R-C(=NOH)NO2], which dissolves in alkali to give an intensely red sodium salt. Therefore, C corresponds to I.
Step 4: Match item D (Hot copper (Cu) catalyst at 573 K with 3° alcohol): Tertiary alcohols lack an alpha-hydrogen atom required for dehydrogenation; over hot copper at 300°C they undergo facile catalytic dehydration to alkenes. Therefore, D corresponds to III.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III, which corresponds to Option A.

subject: Chemistry
questionText:
Match the industrial and laboratory preparations of Phenol in List I with their characteristic reagents and steps in List II:
List I:
A. Cumene (Isopropylbenzene) process
B. Dow's industrial process
C. From Aniline via Diazotization
D. From Benzenesulfonic acid (Alkali fusion)
List II:
I. Chlorobenzene heated with 6-8% aqueous NaOH at 623 K and 300 atm followed by acidification
II. Fusion of sodium benzenesulfonate with solid NaOH at 573-623 K followed by acidification
III. Air oxidation to cumene hydroperoxide followed by dilute H2SO4 cleavage yielding Phenol and Acetone
IV. Reaction with NaNO2 + HCl at 273-278 K followed by warming with water or dilute acid
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Cumene (Isopropylbenzene) process): Autoxidation of cumene gives cumene hydroperoxide; acid treatment catalyzes a phenyl migration to oxygen, breaking the molecule cleanly into phenol and valuable acetone. Therefore, A corresponds to III.
Step 2: Match item B (Dow's industrial process): Under extreme temperature and pressure, chlorobenzene hydrolyzes via an addition-elimination / benzyne pathway to sodium phenoxide, which gives phenol upon acidification. Therefore, B corresponds to I.
Step 3: Match item C (From Aniline via Diazotization): Aniline forms benzenediazonium chloride at 0-5°C; gentle warming with water causes nucleophilic displacement of N2 gas by water, yielding phenol. Therefore, C corresponds to IV.
Step 4: Match item D (From Benzenesulfonic acid (Alkali fusion)): High-temperature fusion displaces the sulfonate group with oxide to form sodium phenoxide and sodium sulfite, affording phenol on acid workup. Therefore, D corresponds to II.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II, which corresponds to Option B.

subject: Chemistry
questionText:
Match the diagnostic chemical tests for Phenols in List I with their observable results in List II:
List I:
A. Phenol + Neutral aqueous FeCl3 solution
B. Phenol + Bromine water [Br2(aq)]
C. Phenol heated with Phthalic anhydride + conc. H2SO4, then poured into NaOH
D. Liebermann's nitroso reaction of phenol
List II:
I. Intense pink / magenta coloration of the indicator Phenolphthalein
II. Characteristic violet / purple coloration due to coordination complex formation
III. Deep blue / green coloration, turning red on dilution with water and restoring blue with excess alkali
IV. Immediate decolourization and precipitation of white 2,4,6-tribromophenol
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Phenol + Neutral aqueous FeCl3 solution): Phenol coordinates to Fe3+ forming a colored hexakis(phenolate)ferrate(III) complex anion [Fe(OC6H5)6]3- with absorption in the visible region. Therefore, A corresponds to II.
Step 2: Match item B (Phenol + Bromine water [Br2(aq)]): In aqueous medium, phenol ionizes significantly to the phenoxide ion, which activates the ring immensely and undergoes rapid electrophilic tribromination at all ortho and para positions. Therefore, B corresponds to IV.
Step 3: Match item C (Phenol heated with Phthalic anhydride + conc. H2SO4, then poured into NaOH): Condensation of two molecules of phenol with phthalic anhydride produces phenolphthalein, which develops a vivid pink color in alkaline solution due to extended quinonoid conjugation. Therefore, C corresponds to I.
Step 4: Match item D (Liebermann's nitroso reaction of phenol): Phenol reacts with nitrous acid to form p-nitrosophenol, which condenses with another phenol molecule to form indophenol, an indicator whose conjugate base is intensely blue. Therefore, D corresponds to III.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III, which corresponds to Option C.

subject: Chemistry
questionText:
Match the Williamson ether synthesis reactants in List I with their primary reaction pathway and product in List II:
List I:
A. Sodium ethoxide (CH3CH2ONa) + Ethyl bromide (CH3CH2Br)
B. Sodium tert-butoxide [(CH3)3CONa] + Methyl iodide (CH3I)
C. Sodium phenoxide (C6H5ONa) + Methyl iodide (CH3I)
D. Sodium ethoxide (CH3CH2ONa) + tert-Butyl bromide [(CH3)3CBr]
List II:
I. tert-Butyl methyl ether (MTBE) formed cleanly via SN2 attack on methyl carbon
II. 2-Methylpropene (Isobutylene) formed exclusively via E2 elimination (zero ether formed)
III. Diethyl ether [(C2H5)2O] formed cleanly via standard bimolecular SN2 substitution
IV. Anisole (Methoxybenzene) formed via SN2 attack of phenoxide on methyl iodide
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Sodium ethoxide (CH3CH2ONa) + Ethyl bromide (CH3CH2Br)): Unshielded primary ethoxide attacks the unhindered primary carbon of bromoethane, displacing bromide via a clean SN2 pathway with minimal elimination. Therefore, A corresponds to III.
Step 2: Match item B (Sodium tert-butoxide [(CH3)3CONa] + Methyl iodide (CH3I)): Methyl iodide possesses zero beta-hydrogens and cannot undergo elimination; the bulky tert-butoxide nucleophile displaces iodide cleanly via backside attack on methyl. Therefore, B corresponds to I.
Step 3: Match item C (Sodium phenoxide (C6H5ONa) + Methyl iodide (CH3I)): Phenoxide is an effective nucleophile that displaces iodide from methyl iodide cleanly, yielding the aromatic ether anisole without side-reactions. Therefore, C corresponds to IV.
Step 4: Match item D (Sodium ethoxide (CH3CH2ONa) + tert-Butyl bromide [(CH3)3CBr]): Strongly basic ethoxide encounters severe steric crowding at the tertiary carbon; instead of substitution, it abstracts a beta-proton to trigger rapid E2 elimination. Therefore, D corresponds to II.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II, which corresponds to Option D.

subject: Chemistry
questionText:
Match the ether cleavage reactions with concentrated Hydroiodic acid (HI) in List I with their stoichiometric products in List II:
List I:
A. Anisole (Methoxybenzene) + 1 equivalent of HI heated
B. tert-Butyl ethyl ether + 1 equivalent of cold HI
C. Methyl isopropyl ether + 1 equivalent of cold HI
D. Diethyl ether + excess concentrated HI heated
List II:
I. Propan-2-ol (Isopropyl alcohol) and Methyl iodide (CH3I)
II. tert-Butyl iodide [(CH3)3CI] and Ethanol (CH3CH2OH)
III. 2 equivalents of Ethyl iodide (CH3CH2I) and 1 equivalent of Water
IV. Phenol (C6H5OH) and Methyl iodide (CH3I)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Anisole (Methoxybenzene) + 1 equivalent of HI heated): Protonation yields methylphenyl oxonium ion. The phenyl C-O bond has partial double-bond character due to resonance and cannot be cleaved; iodide attacks the methyl carbon via SN2 to yield phenol and CH3I. Therefore, A corresponds to IV.
Step 2: Match item B (tert-Butyl ethyl ether + 1 equivalent of cold HI): Cleavage proceeds through an SN1 mechanism because the tertiary tert-butyl carbocation is exceptionally stable; heterolysis yields (CH3)3C+ which captures iodide, leaving ethanol. Therefore, B corresponds to II.
Step 3: Match item C (Methyl isopropyl ether + 1 equivalent of cold HI): Both groups are primary/secondary; cleavage proceeds through an SN2 pathway where iodide attacks the less sterically hindered methyl carbon preferentially. Therefore, C corresponds to I.
Step 4: Match item D (Diethyl ether + excess concentrated HI heated): First step yields ethyl iodide and ethanol; under excess hot HI, ethanol is protonated and converted into a second equivalent of ethyl iodide via nucleophilic substitution. Therefore, D corresponds to III.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III, which corresponds to Option A.

subject: Chemistry
questionText:
Match the epoxide ring-opening reactions in List I with their regiochemical products and pathway descriptions in List II:
List I:
A. 2,2-Dimethyloxirane (Isobutylene oxide) + CH3OH in the presence of trace H2SO4 (acidic)
B. 2,2-Dimethyloxirane + Sodium methoxide (CH3ONa) in CH3OH (basic/nucleophilic)
C. 2-Methyloxirane (Propylene oxide) + HBr (acidic)
D. Styrene oxide + Lithium aluminum hydride (LiAlH4) followed by H3O+
List II:
I. 1-Methoxy-2-methylpropan-2-ol formed by nucleophilic attack at the less substituted primary carbon
II. 1-Phenylethanol formed by hydride attack at the primary CH2 carbon
III. 2-Methoxy-2-methylpropan-1-ol formed by nucleophilic attack at the more substituted tertiary carbon
IV. 1-Bromo-2-propanol formed predominantly by bromide attack at the more substituted secondary carbon
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (2,2-Dimethyloxirane (Isobutylene oxide) + CH3OH in the presence of trace H2SO4 (acidic)): Under acidic conditions, the epoxide oxygen is protonated; the C-O bond to the tertiary carbon weakens substantially, developing significant carbocation character, directing nucleophile attack to C-2. Therefore, A corresponds to III.
Step 2: Match item B (2,2-Dimethyloxirane + Sodium methoxide (CH3ONa) in CH3OH (basic/nucleophilic)): Under basic conditions, the strong methoxide nucleophile attacks the epoxide ring via a pure SN2 mechanism, attacking exclusively at the less sterically hindered primary carbon. Therefore, B corresponds to I.
Step 3: Match item C (2-Methyloxirane (Propylene oxide) + HBr (acidic)): Protonation of the oxygen atom polarizes the ring; partial positive charge develops preferentially at the secondary carbon, which is attacked by bromide. Therefore, C corresponds to IV.
Step 4: Match item D (Styrene oxide + Lithium aluminum hydride (LiAlH4) followed by H3O+): Hydride from LiAlH4 acts as a powerful unhindered nucleophile under basic conditions, attacking the less substituted terminal CH2 group via SN2 to leave the benzylic alcohol. Therefore, D corresponds to II.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II, which corresponds to Option B.

subject: Chemistry
questionText:
Match the oxidation reagents in List I with their selective action on alcohols in List II:
List I:
A. Pyridinium chlorochromate (PCC) in anhydrous CH2Cl2
B. Jones reagent (CrO3 in aqueous H2SO4 and acetone)
C. Active Manganese dioxide (MnO2) in acetone
D. Vapors of tert-Butanol passed over heated Copper at 573 K
List II:
I. Selectively oxidizes allylic and benzylic alcohols while leaving saturated aliphatic alcohols untouched
II. Oxidizes 1° alcohols selectively to Aldehydes without over-oxidation to carboxylic acids
III. Undergoes catalytic dehydration to 2-Methylpropene (Isobutylene) instead of dehydrogenation
IV. Oxidizes 1° alcohols to Carboxylic acids and 2° alcohols to Ketones rapidly
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Pyridinium chlorochromate (PCC) in anhydrous CH2Cl2): PCC operates under strictly anhydrous non-aqueous conditions; because water is absent, the aldehyde cannot form a gem-diol hydrate, preventing further oxidation to carboxylic acid. Therefore, A corresponds to II.
Step 2: Match item B (Jones reagent (CrO3 in aqueous H2SO4 and acetone)): In the presence of aqueous acid, the intermediate aldehyde forms a chromate ester through its gem-diol hydrate, undergoing immediate oxidation to a carboxylic acid. Therefore, B corresponds to IV.
Step 3: Match item C (Active Manganese dioxide (MnO2) in acetone): MnO2 is a mild heterogeneous oxidant whose radical mechanism selectively abstracts weak benzylic or allylic C-H bonds, preserving simple aliphatic hydroxyl groups. Therefore, C corresponds to I.
Step 4: Match item D (Vapors of tert-Butanol passed over heated Copper at 573 K): Tertiary alcohols lack an alpha-hydrogen atom needed for carbonyl formation; heated copper acts as a mild Lewis acid catalyst, promoting E1 dehydration to alkene. Therefore, D corresponds to III.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III, which corresponds to Option C.

subject: Chemistry
questionText:
Match the named reactions of Phenol in List I with their principal products and reaction conditions in List II:
List I:
A. Kolbe-Schmitt reaction: Phenol + NaOH + CO2 at 400 K and 4-7 atm followed by H3O+
B. Reimer-Tiemann reaction: Phenol + CHCl3 + aqueous KOH at 340 K followed by H3O+
C. Azo coupling: Phenol + Benzenediazonium chloride at pH 9-10 and 273-278 K
D. Nitration of Phenol with dilute HNO3 at 298 K
List II:
I. Salicylaldehyde (2-hydroxybenzaldehyde) formed via electrophilic attack of :CCl2 carbene
II. Mixture of ortho- and para-nitrophenol, easily separable by steam distillation
III. Salicylic acid (2-hydroxybenzoic acid) formed via electrophilic carboxylation of phenoxide
IV. p-Hydroxyazobenzene (orange azo dye) formed via electrophilic aromatic substitution
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Kolbe-Schmitt reaction: Phenol + NaOH + CO2 at 400 K and 4-7 atm followed by H3O+): Sodium phenoxide reacts with weak electrophile CO2; chelation of sodium ion with carbonyl oxygen directs electrophilic attack specifically to the ortho position to yield salicylic acid. Therefore, A corresponds to III.
Step 2: Match item B (Reimer-Tiemann reaction: Phenol + CHCl3 + aqueous KOH at 340 K followed by H3O+): Dichlorocarbene generated in situ from chloroform attacks the activated phenoxide ring at the ortho position; alkaline hydrolysis of the resulting benzal chloride intermediate gives salicylaldehyde. Therefore, B corresponds to I.
Step 3: Match item C (Azo coupling: Phenol + Benzenediazonium chloride at pH 9-10 and 273-278 K): In weakly alkaline medium, phenol exists as phenoxide, which couples with benzenediazonium ion at the unhindered para position to form a brightly colored conjugated azo dye. Therefore, C corresponds to IV.
Step 4: Match item D (Nitration of Phenol with dilute HNO3 at 298 K): Dilute nitric acid mononitrates phenol at room temperature; ortho-nitrophenol is steam-volatile due to intramolecular H-bonding, whereas para-nitrophenol has intermolecular H-bonding. Therefore, D corresponds to II.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II, which corresponds to Option D.

subject: Chemistry
questionText:
Match the alcohol dehydration reactions in List I with their major alkene product and rearrangement mechanism in List II:
List I:
A. 3,3-Dimethylbutan-2-ol heated with conc. H2SO4
B. Butan-2-ol heated with 85% H3PO4 at 373 K
C. Cyclopentylmethanol heated with concentrated acid
D. Ethanol heated with concentrated H2SO4 at 443 K (170°C)
List II:
I. Cyclohexene formed as major product via Wagner-Meerwein ring expansion
II. trans-But-2-ene formed as major disubstituted alkene following Zaitsev's rule
III. Ethene (CH2=CH2) formed via bimolecular or unimolecular elimination of protonated ethanol
IV. 2,3-Dimethylbut-2-ene formed as major tetrasubstituted alkene via 1,2-methide shift
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (3,3-Dimethylbutan-2-ol heated with conc. H2SO4): Protonation and loss of water yields a 2° carbocation [(CH3)3C-CH(+)-CH3]; rapid 1,2-methyl shift creates the more stable 3° carbocation [(CH3)2C(+)-CH(CH3)2], followed by Zaitsev elimination. Therefore, A corresponds to IV.
Step 2: Match item B (Butan-2-ol heated with 85% H3PO4 at 373 K): Dehydration via a secondary butyl carbocation produces but-2-ene as the thermodynamic product, with trans favored over cis due to minimal steric hindrance. Therefore, B corresponds to II.
Step 3: Match item C (Cyclopentylmethanol heated with concentrated acid): Loss of water gives a primary cyclobutylcarbinyl-like carbocation; migration of an endocyclic C-C sigma bond expands the 5-membered ring into a strain-free 6-membered cyclohexyl cation. Therefore, C corresponds to I.
Step 4: Match item D (Ethanol heated with concentrated H2SO4 at 443 K (170°C)): At 443 K, beta-elimination dominates to produce ethene gas; at lower temperature (413 K), nucleophilic substitution by a second ethanol molecule produces diethyl ether. Therefore, D corresponds to III.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III, which corresponds to Option A.

subject: Chemistry
questionText:
Match the substituted phenols in List I with their relative acidity (pKa values) and electronic rationale in List II:
List I:
A. 4-Nitrophenol (para-Nitrophenol)
B. 3-Nitrophenol (meta-Nitrophenol)
C. Phenol (unsubstituted)
D. 4-Methylphenol (para-Cresol)
List II:
I. pKa ~ 8.36; moderately acidic due to -I effect only (mesomeric -M cannot operate from meta)
II. pKa ~ 10.26; less acidic than phenol due to electron donation by hyperconjugation and +I
III. pKa ~ 7.15; strongly acidic due to powerful combined -M and -I electron delocalization
IV. pKa ~ 9.95; baseline reference acidity stabilized by phenyl ring resonance delocalization
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (4-Nitrophenol (para-Nitrophenol)): The para-nitro group can participate in direct through-resonance with the phenoxide negative charge, placing electron density directly onto the electronegative nitro oxygen atoms. Therefore, A corresponds to III.
Step 2: Match item B (3-Nitrophenol (meta-Nitrophenol)): At the meta position, the nitro group cannot directly conjugate with the phenoxide negative charge; stabilization of the phenoxide occurs solely through inductive electron withdrawal. Therefore, B corresponds to I.
Step 3: Match item C (Phenol (unsubstituted)): Phenol is substantially more acidic than aliphatic alcohols because phenoxide negative charge is resonance-delocalized over the ortho and para positions of the aromatic ring. Therefore, C corresponds to IV.
Step 4: Match item D (4-Methylphenol (para-Cresol)): The methyl group donates electron density into the ring through hyperconjugation and inductive effect, increasing electron density on oxygen and destabilizing the phenoxide anion. Therefore, D corresponds to II.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II, which corresponds to Option B.

subject: Chemistry
questionText:
Match the reduction transformations yielding alcohols in List I with their selective reducing agents in List II:
List I:
A. Ethyl benzoate (C6H5COOCH2CH3) reduced to Benzyl alcohol and Ethanol
B. Acetophenone (C6H5COCH3) reduced to 1-Phenylethanol
C. Crotonaldehyde (CH3-CH=CH-CHO) reduced selectively to Crotyl alcohol (CH3-CH=CH-CH2OH)
D. Cyclohex-2-enone reduced selectively to Cyclohex-2-enol
List II:
I. Sodium borohydride (NaBH4) in ethanol at low temperature
II. Lithium aluminum hydride (LiAlH4) in dry ether followed by acidic workup
III. Diisobutylaluminum hydride (DIBAL-H) at -78°C or Luche reagent (NaBH4 / CeCl3)
IV. Sodium borohydride (NaBH4) in ethanol at room temperature
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Ethyl benzoate (C6H5COOCH2CH3) reduced to Benzyl alcohol and Ethanol): LiAlH4 is a powerful nucleophilic hydride donor capable of reducing esters cleanly to primary alcohols; milder reducing agents like NaBH4 are completely unreactive toward esters. Therefore, A corresponds to II.
Step 2: Match item B (Acetophenone (C6H5COCH3) reduced to 1-Phenylethanol): NaBH4 is a mild and chemoselective reducing agent that rapidly reduces ketones and aldehydes to alcohols without reducing esters, amides, or carboxylic acids. Therefore, B corresponds to IV.
Step 3: Match item C (Crotonaldehyde (CH3-CH=CH-CHO) reduced selectively to Crotyl alcohol (CH3-CH=CH-CH2OH)): NaBH4 selectively reduces the carbonyl group of alpha,beta-unsaturated aldehydes via 1,2-addition, preserving the conjugated carbon-carbon double bond intact. Therefore, C corresponds to I.
Step 4: Match item D (Cyclohex-2-enone reduced selectively to Cyclohex-2-enol): Luche reduction or controlled DIBAL-H reduction cleanly conducts 1,2-hydride addition to the enone carbonyl, avoiding conjugate 1,4-reduction of the alkene. Therefore, D corresponds to III.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III, which corresponds to Option C.

subject: Chemistry
questionText:
Match the vicinal polyols and alpha-hydroxy compounds in List I with their oxidative cleavage products with Periodic acid (HIO4) in List II:
List I:
A. Ethane-1,2-diol (Ethylene glycol) + 1 mole of HIO4
B. Propane-1,2,3-triol (Glycerol) + 2 moles of HIO4
C. Pinacol (2,3-dimethylbutane-2,3-diol) + 1 mole of HIO4
D. Benzoin [C6H5-CH(OH)-CO-C6H5] + 1 mole of HIO4
List II:
I. 2 moles of Formaldehyde (HCHO) and 1 mole of Methanoic acid (Formic acid, HCOOH)
II. 1 mole of Benzaldehyde (C6H5CHO) and 1 mole of Benzoic acid (C6H5COOH)
III. 2 moles of Methanal (Formaldehyde, HCHO)
IV. 2 moles of Propan-2-one (Acetone)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Ethane-1,2-diol (Ethylene glycol) + 1 mole of HIO4): Periodic acid cleaves the C-C bond of 1,2-diols via a cyclic periodate ester intermediate; each primary alcohol carbon is oxidized to formaldehyde. Therefore, A corresponds to III.
Step 2: Match item B (Propane-1,2,3-triol (Glycerol) + 2 moles of HIO4): Glycerol has two adjacent vicinal diol linkages, requiring 2 moles of HIO4; the two terminal 1° carbons yield formaldehyde, while the central 2° carbon is oxidized to formic acid. Therefore, B corresponds to I.
Step 3: Match item C (Pinacol (2,3-dimethylbutane-2,3-diol) + 1 mole of HIO4): Cleavage of the central C-C bond between the two tertiary alcohol carbons oxidizes both carbinol centers to acetone molecules. Therefore, C corresponds to IV.
Step 4: Match item D (Benzoin [C6H5-CH(OH)-CO-C6H5] + 1 mole of HIO4): HIO4 cleaves alpha-hydroxy ketones cleanly: the secondary alcohol carbon is oxidized to an aldehyde, while the carbonyl carbon is oxidized to a carboxylic acid. Therefore, D corresponds to II.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II, which corresponds to Option D.

subject: Chemistry
questionText:
Match the pinacol-pinacolone rearrangement systems in List I with their mechanistic pathway and dominant ketone product in List II:
List I:
A. 1,2-Diphenylpropane-1,2-diol treated with concentrated H2SO4
B. 1,1-Diphenyl-2-methylpropane-1,2-diol treated with acid
C. 1-(p-Methoxyphenyl)-1-phenylethane-1,2-diol treated with acid
D. 1,1'-Bicyclopentyl-1,1'-diol treated with concentrated acid
List II:
I. p-Anisyl group migrates faster than phenyl group by a factor of ~500
II. 3,3-Diphenylbutan-2-one formed via regioselective carbocation formation and methyl migration
III. Spiro[4.5]decan-6-one formed via pinacol rearrangement with ring expansion
IV. 1,1-Diphenylpropan-2-one formed via preferential phenyl migration over methyl
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (1,2-Diphenylpropane-1,2-diol treated with concentrated H2SO4): Protonation occurs preferentially at the tertiary benzylic carbon to generate the more stable benzylic cation; migration of the phenyl group occurs faster than methyl due to superior migratory aptitude. Therefore, A corresponds to IV.
Step 2: Match item B (1,1-Diphenyl-2-methylpropane-1,2-diol treated with acid): Protonation and water loss occurs selectively at the carbon with two phenyl groups to form a resonance-stabilized benzhydryl cation; 1,2-methyl shift follows to give an oxocarbenium ion. Therefore, B corresponds to II.
Step 3: Match item C (1-(p-Methoxyphenyl)-1-phenylethane-1,2-diol treated with acid): The strong electron-donating (+M) methoxy group stabilizes the developing positive charge in the bridged phenonium ion transition state, dramatically accelerating aryl migration. Therefore, C corresponds to I.
Step 4: Match item D (1,1'-Bicyclopentyl-1,1'-diol treated with concentrated acid): Protonation and dehydration of one cyclopentyl carbinol creates a tertiary carbocation; migration of an adjacent ring C-C bond expands one cyclopentane into a cyclohexane, yielding a spiro ketone. Therefore, D corresponds to III.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III, which corresponds to Option A.

subject: Chemistry
questionText:
Match the thermal and Lewis acid-catalyzed rearrangements of phenol derivatives in List I with their reaction characteristics in List II:
List I:
A. Phenyl acetate + anhydrous AlCl3 at 298 K (room temperature)
B. Phenyl acetate + anhydrous AlCl3 at 433 K (160°C)
C. Allyl phenyl ether heated to 473 K (200°C) without catalyst
D. Allyl 2,6-dimethylphenyl ether heated to 473 K
List II:
I. 2-Hydroxyacetophenone (ortho-isomer) formed as major product under thermodynamic control
